summary: Onboarding tour (backend and front-end wiring): a read-only-for-the-person's-data demo project (pdh-demo) served from a throw-away offline SQLite sandbox built from a built-in fixture (29 public arXiv Transformer-lineage papers: 5 unrated candidates + 24 earlier records spread over four weeks, with categories, pinned-term history and pre-written zh/en previews); request routing by header X-PDH-Demo or project_id with an allow list and a 403 demo_readonly for everything else; /api/onboarding (state, start, done) with state in onboarding.json; /api/projects carries a demo descriptor; app_version.current(); first-run assertions in the packaged-backend verifier. Front end: tour.js/tour.css wired into the main, settings, weekly and creation pages; api() sends the demo header only while the demo is current; the demo id is never stored; demo mode hides every entry that would fetch, call a model, read a PDF or edit; settings 'replay tour'; creation page offers 'see the demo' when there is no project.
scope_note: Worktree onboarding-tour, second commit(s) on top of the no-default-project commit; The backend (aecdac5) and tour.js/tour.css (38e8b1e) are already committed; 'files' lists only what this commit changes. Includes the coordinator's verbatim-abstract fixture (app/demo_fixture.py, harness/sources.json). The demo makes zero model calls and zero network requests.

budget_impact.rationale: The demo triage writes pre-written previews (model=demo); no provider is called, no prompt registered, no retry. The sandbox gateway cannot call a model even with DEEPSEEK_API_KEY set.
budget_impact.after: demo with zero tokens and no network

open_risks: The organization worker lock is global: a demo graph job and a real organization job exclude each other (the loser gets 'already running').
A request that sends X-PDH-Demo gets the sandbox for every non-settings route; the page must send the header only while the tour is on screen.
Windows cannot delete an open sandbox file; the old generation then stays until the next reset (tested by simulating a failed delete, not on Windows).
Direction names in the sandbox library are written in the language chosen at reset time; switching the interface language mid-tour does not rename them.

NOT verified in a browser: tour.js's DOM layer (spotlight, bubble, waiting for targets, cross-page resume) has never run in any browser; the 16-step walk, skip, reload, English, dark theme and the real-database-empty check after a browser run are open (preview tool reads the main checkout's launch.json; headless Chrome blocked by the sandbox). E-ONBOARDING needs native macOS and Windows packaged runs anyway.
sessionStorage survival across page loads in WKWebView / WebView2 is an inference.
Selector dependence: tour steps target ids/classes in index.html, settings.html, organization.js and profile-ui.js; a renamed element degrades to a centred bubble after 15 s rather than blocking.
